content: Your doctor has prescribed dalteparin sodium, an anticoagulant commonly referred to as a blood thinner, to prevent the formation of harmful blood clots. This medication will be administered as an injection under the skin (subcutaneously) once daily. In some cases, dalteparin may be prescribed for other uses, so you should consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Your healthcare provider (doctor, nurse, or pharmacist) may monitor the effectiveness of the treatment and check for side effects through laboratory tests and physical examinations. It is crucial to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. The duration of your treatment will depend on how your body responds to the medication. Precautions Before starting dalteparin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to dalteparin, heparin, enoxaparin (Lovenox), any other medications, or pork products. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including those mentioned in the Important Warning section, as well as any vitamins or supplements. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver or kidney disease or diabetes. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking dalteparin, contact your doctor immediately. Administering Your Medication Before administering dalteparin, carefully inspect the solution. It should appear clear and free of any floating particles. Check the container for leaks. Do not use the solution if it is discolored, contains particles, or if the container is damaged or leaking. Use a new solution instead, but show the damaged one to your healthcare provider. It is essential to follow your healthcare provider's instructions precisely when using this medication. Do not alter your dosing schedule without consulting your healthcare provider. Side Effects Dalteparin may cause side effects. Notify your healthcare provider if you experience a severe or persistent upset stomach. If you encounter any of the following symptoms or those listed in the Important Warning section, contact your doctor or healthcare provider immediately: Unusual bleeding Vomiting or coughing up blood, or material resembling coffee grounds Bloody or black, tarry stools Blood in your urine Red or dark-brown urine Easy bruising Excessive menstrual bleeding Fever Dizziness or lightheadedness If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Storing Your Medication Your healthcare provider will likely supply you with several days' worth of dalteparin at a time. You will be instructed to store it at room temperature. Follow the storage instructions carefully to ensure the medication remains effective. Keep your supplies in a clean, dry place when not in use, and store all medications and supplies out of reach of children. Your healthcare provider will provide guidance on how to safely dispose of used needles, syringes, tubing, and containers to prevent accidental injury. In Case of Emergency or Overdose If you suspect an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911 immediately. Signs of Infection If you are receiving dalteparin injections under your skin, it is important to recognize the symptoms of a catheter-related infection (an infection at the site where the needle enters your skin).
